_comment: Hand-written reveal for dev/reveal.html. Every optional round_reveal field is present. trivia.facts holds the v1.3 structured trivia: 4 real, verified literature facts for mmus_l5_et copied from neuroguesser-content/content/types/facts/mmus_l5_et.yaml (one each of category function, identify (contrast_with_labels + a support quote), connectivity and other); trivia_v12_facts (outside the reveal) keeps the earlier uncategorised dev stand-ins for the page's "Trivia: v1.2" switch. Type and option labels are the type cards' display labels. Validated against neuroguesser-content/contracts (round_reveal v1.3, round_public, round_state, ephys_trace, graph_clue). Asset paths are content-hash shaped; dev/reveal.js serves the JSON ones from 'assets' and swaps the GLBs for a closed fixture day's when the dev Worker is up.

same_cell_function.summary: Dev fixture. This very cell was imaged in vivo before the EM: its responses to drifting gratings were orientation tuned.

facts.text: Motion detectors: with one grating protocol in mouse visual cortex, 60% of these subcortically projecting layer 5 cells were very sharply direction-tuned, versus under 30% of the two other layer 5 types tested.
facts.quote: L5 CS PNs were remarkably direction selective and non-parametric statistical tests showed that Glt25d2-Cre + neurons have higher DSI (median 0.57) than Tlx3-Cre + (median 0.24, Kruskal-Wallis test p=0.0024, with Dunn's multiple comparisons, Tlx3-Cre + versus Glt25d2-Cre + , p = 0.0135). 60% of Glt25d2-Cre + cells were very sharply tuned for direction (DSI > 0.5) while less than 30% of Tlx3-Cre + or L5 Efr3a-Cre + cells had DSI > 0.5

facts.text: Long in every compartment: in mouse visual cortex, ET cells (about 17% of layer 5) sit in its deeper half and have longer apical, basal and oblique dendrites than other layer 5 cells; NP cells have little or no obliques.
facts.quote: also known as extratelencephalic (ET) projection neurons. These cells accounted for approximately 17% of the cells within L5 (based on a classifier trained on a smaller, manually annotated subset of the data; see Methods). They were restricted almost exclusively to the deeper half of L5 (Fig. 5 A L5 a and d, inset 2; C inset top right), and compared to other L5 cells, they have the longest skeleton for all three dendritic compartments: apical, basal, and oblique.

support.quote: Another morphologically distinct type of cell was apparent at the end of the layer 5 spectrum: the near-projecting (NP) cells 7 , 25 with their long and sparse basal dendrites (Fig. 5 A L5 d, inset 3). These cells accounted for approximately 4% of the cells within L5. They tended to send their dendrites deeper (relative to the soma), had little or no obliques, and tended to have small or no apical tufts.

facts.text: A feedback loop: in a mouse visual cortex connectome, the local axons of these thick-tufted cells primarily contact a group of inhibitory cell types that, in turn, specifically target them back.
facts.quote: This study investigates the connectivity of mouse visual cortex thick tufted layer 5 pyramidal cells, also known as extratelencephalic neurons (L5-ETns), using a 1 mm 3 publicly available electron microscopy dataset. The analysis reveals that, in their immediate vicinity, L5-ETns primarily establish connections with a group of inhibitory cell types, which, in turn, specifically target the L5-ETns back.

facts.text: A developmental tug-of-war: mouse mutants provided evidence that the transcription factor Fezf2 blocks corticothalamic fate in layer 5 subcerebral neurons by reducing Tbr1 expression.
facts.citation: McKenna et al. 2011, The Journal of Neuroscience
facts.quote: Analysis of Fezf2 mutants and Tbr1 −/− ; Fezf2 −/− compound mutants provided evidence that Fezf2 blocks corticothalamic fate in layer 5 by reducing Tbr1 expression in subcerebral neurons.

papers.citation: McKenna et al. 2011, The Journal of Neuroscience

trivia_v12_facts.text: Layer 5 extratelencephalic cells send their axons out of the cortex, to targets such as the thalamus, midbrain, pons and spinal cord (dev fixture fact).
trivia_v12_facts.quote: Dev fixture stand-in for the verbatim supporting sentence. In a real reveal this is the exact sentence from the paper that the bake matched against the fetched full text before the fact could ship.

trivia_v12_facts.text: Their thick apical dendrite climbs to layer 1 and ends in a wide tuft, which is why they are also called thick-tufted cells (dev fixture fact).
trivia_v12_facts.quote: Dev fixture stand-in for the verbatim supporting sentence copied word for word from the source.

trivia_v12_facts.text: They are a minority of the excitatory cells in a cortical column; intratelencephalic cells, whose axons stay in the forebrain, are far more common (dev fixture fact).
